samples.summary: New `removeLabel` gives fork-controlled artifact data a destructive privileged write: a PR can make the App-token reporter delete its own `ci-config-changed` warning
samples.evidence: `areas` (ci-report.yml:157) is parsed from `ci-context/areas.json`, an artifact produced at ci.yml:105 by `node ./scripts/changed-areas.mjs` running from the PULL REQUEST's checkout — for `pull_request` the workflow definition AND the resolver script both come from the head branch, so the JSON is entirely author-controlled. Before this change the label was add-only, so a lying resolver could only fail to raise the alarm. Line 284 turns that into an active erasure: a PR that edits `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `harness.config.json` or `scripts/changed-areas.mjs` can emit `{"full":true,...,"ciConfig":false}` (full suite still runs, so all required checks stay green and nothing looks off) and the privileged `workflow_run` job — holding an App installation token scoped `issues: write` (ci-report.yml:95-107) — removes `ci-config-changed` from the PR, including a label a maintainer added by hand. Per harness.config.json:50 and .github/CODEOWNERS:50-52 this label plus the job-summary warning are the *human* half of the CI-gating guard, and CODEOWNERS only blocks a merge when 'Require review from Code Owners' is enabled. A guard whose alarm the alarmed-about change can delete is worse than no alarm.

samples.summary: IDOR: the target PR number is read unvalidated from a fork-controlled artifact, and the diff extends that primitive from comment writes to label deletion on any issue/PR
samples.evidence: `prNumber` comes from `ci-context/pr-number`, written by a step in `ci.yml` (lines 155-173) that executes from the PR's own head branch, so a fork contributor can write ANY issue number there. `ci-report.yml` never cross-checks it against `run.pull_requests` or `listPullRequestsAssociatedWithCommit(run.head_sha)` — those are only consulted when the artifact value is missing (lines 143-151). With the App token (`issues: write`) the reporter then acts on that arbitrary number: it created/updated a comment before (lines 246-254) and, as of this diff, also calls `github.rest.issues.removeLabel({ issue_number: prNumber, name: 'ci-config-changed' })` at line 284. Attack: open a PR (workflow-run approval is only required for first-time contributors by default), edit ci.yml in the head branch to `printf '%s' "999" > "$CONTEXT_DIR/pr-number"` and craft areas.json, and the trusted App identity forges a verification comment on issue/PR #999 and strips its `ci-config-changed` label. The `.catch()` at line 286 swallows the 404s that probing a wrong number would otherwise surface.

samples.summary: Label removal fires on fail-safe resolutions: `ciConfig: false` also means "the resolver gave up", so an attacker-triggerable failure clears a truthful warning
samples.evidence: Every fail-safe path in `scripts/changed-areas.mjs` returns `FULL(...)` (line 470-477) with `ciConfig: false` — 'no diff base could be resolved', 'could not diff X...Y', 'could not read the CI mapping', 'WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS was not a resolution object', unmapped paths (line 425-432). All of those parse as a resolution, so `else if (areas)` at ci-report.yml:280 removes `ci-config-changed` even though the resolver never determined what changed. The comment at 281-283 claims the guard is 'only when `areas` parsed', which does not distinguish 'nothing gating changed' from 'unknown'. A PR that edits gating files can reach this deterministically (e.g. make its resolver throw, or make the diff fail), so the same suppression as the finding above is available without even having to lie about `ciConfig`. Fail-safe must stay fail-safe in BOTH directions: the correct behaviour is to leave the label alone unless the resolver actually classified the diff (e.g. gate removal on `areas.full === false || areas.reasons`-derived success).

samples.summary: The reduced-run gate is computed by code from the PR under review, so the documented "a PR cannot grade its own homework" property does not hold and a lying resolver yields three green required checks with nothing executed
samples.evidence: harness.config.json:50 states 'the reduced-run decision is always made by the version of the mapping already on main'. It is not: the `changes` job checks out the PR (default ref = merge ref, i.e. head content) and runs the PR's own `scripts/changed-areas.mjs` and `harness.config.json`. A resolver that emits `{"full":false,"heavy":false,"packages":[],"tags":[],"ciConfig":false}` makes `verify-self` select zero lanes while still reporting `verify-self (22.x)` success, and `verify-browser`/`verify-integration` no-op every step by design (ci.yml:434, 556) yet report success under the required matrix names — three green required contexts with nothing verified. `ciConfig` was the compensating control precisely because it is the loud signal a reviewer sees; this diff makes that signal removable by the same untrusted data (see the removeLabel findings), so the compensation weakens exactly where it is needed. Mitigation is a human approving review, which is what the label exists to inform.

samples.summary: `baseBranchTip`'s ref validation accepts `..` and a leading `-`, feeding them into `git rev-parse` argument positions
samples.evidence: `/^[\w./-]+$/` admits `../../heads/x` (ref-namespace traversal when interpolated into `refs/remotes/origin/${baseRef}` at line 245) and admits values starting with `-`, which git may parse as an option in the third candidate `git rev-parse --verify "${ref}^{commit}"` (line 246, `ref === baseRef`). Exploitation is currently blocked downstream because `verified()` re-runs `rev-parse --verify` on whatever comes back, so an option-printed string cannot become a base; and `base.ref` is a branch of the base repository (ci.yml restricts PRs to `main`), so it is not directly attacker-chosen. Hardening: require `^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*(/[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*)*$` and reject `..` explicitly, or pass `--end-of-options`.

samples.summary: `changedPaths` interpolates its refs straight into a `git diff` argument while the verification that makes that safe lives in a different exported function
samples.evidence: `git diff --name-only "${base}...${head}"` with no `--end-of-options` and no local validation. `changedPaths` is an exported entry point whose refs are only guaranteed to be verified shas when they came from `resolveRefs`; a future or test caller passing e.g. `base = '--output=/tmp/x'` would produce the argument `--output=/tmp/x...HEAD`, which git parses as `--output=<file>` — an arbitrary file write. Not reachable today (resolve() at line 545-548 is the only production caller and every ref passes `verified()`), but the guard and the sink are now in separate functions, so the safety property is no longer local to the sink. Add `"--end-of-options"` before the range, or assert `/^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$|^HEAD$/` inside `changedPaths`.

verdict.reason: The described code is present and reachable exactly as claimed. ci-report.yml:274-293 calls issues.removeLabel('ci-config-changed') whenever the parsed `areas` has a falsy `ciConfig`; `areas` is read at ci-report.yml:157 from the `ci-context` artifact, which ci.yml:103-105,155-173 produces by running scripts/changed-areas.mjs from the pull request's own checkout (for `pull_request`, both ci.yml and the resolver come from the head branch), and ci-report.yml:114-122 itself declares that artifact attacker-controlled. The write uses an App installation token scoped `issues: write` (ci-report.yml:95-107) in a privileged workflow_run job (ci-report.yml:38-41,64), so a PR touching .github/workflows/**, .github/CODEOWNERS, harness.config.json or scripts/changed-areas.mjs can emit ciConfig:false (while still reporting full:true so required checks stay green) and have the reporter delete the warning label, including one a maintainer applied by hand. harness.config.json:50 and .github/CODEOWNERS:50-52 confirm the label is the intentionally independent human half of the CI-gating guard and that CODEOWNERS only binds when 'Require review from Code Owners' is enabled, so nothing else makes this unreachable. Untrusted input driving a destructive privileged write that suppresses a review/authorization alarm is in the security lane; major severity stands.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo; the code matches the finding. ci-report.yml:139-151 takes prNumber from the ci-context/pr-number artifact and consults run.pull_requests / listPullRequestsAssociatedWithCommit ONLY as fallbacks when the artifact value is absent — there is no cross-check of the artifact value against the run's real PR. That artifact is written by ci.yml:155-173, a pull_request-triggered workflow (ci.yml:9) whose file executes from the PR head ref, so a fork contributor can edit the printf at ci.yml:164 (and craft areas.json via scripts/changed-areas.mjs at ci.yml:163) to emit any issue number. The consuming job runs with the App installation token scoped to issues: write (ci-report.yml:95-107) and feeds that number to listComments (247), createComment (253), addLabels (278) and, as of this diff, removeLabel (284) — a destructive write on an arbitrary issue/PR. Failures are swallowed: the .catch at 286-289 drops 404s and the outer catch at 291-293 downgrades the rest to core.warning, so probing is silent. No guard makes this unreachable: the only gate is workflow_run.event == 'pull_request' (ci-report.yml:64); every other privileged workflow_run consumer carries a fork-origin check (docker-publish.yml:71, publish-ghpage.yml:46, agent-iterate-ci.yml:52, agent-review-panel.yml:163) but ci-report.yml intentionally has none because serving fork PRs is its purpose. The design doc acknowledges artifact contents are attacker-controlled (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:353-357) but addresses only markdown sanitization, never the PR number (350-352). This is a confused-deputy IDOR, squarely in the authorization/access-control lane, and is blocking.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. FULL() (scripts/changed-areas.mjs:470-477) emits ciConfig:false for every fail-safe give-up path — invalid JSON (515), not-a-resolution (525), unreadable CI mapping (542), no diff base (546), diff failure (550) — plus the unmapped-path bail-out (425-432). All satisfy isResolution (489-498) and parse as JSON, so they fall into the `else if (areas)` branch at .github/workflows/ci-report.yml:280 and call removeLabel for ci-config-changed (284-289) even though the resolver never classified the diff. The comment at 281-283 only distinguishes "artifact missing" from "artifact parsed", not "unknown" from "no gating change", exactly as claimed. Reachable by a PR author: areas.json is produced by running the PR's own resolver in the changes job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:105, uploaded 155-173), and harness.config.json is itself a gating file (harness.config.json:51-61), so a PR that edits it into a shape readCiConfig rejects (changed-areas.mjs:86-93) yields FULL("could not read the CI mapping") with ciConfig:false and clears a truthful label. In lane because the label is the visible/review half of the CI-gating guard, relied on precisely because CODEOWNERS only binds when branch protection enables Code Owner review (harness.config.json:50; .github/CODEOWNERS:8-26,37-52). No guard elsewhere makes the removal unreachable, so no refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence checks out line by line. harness.config.json:50 documents that "the reduced-run decision is always made by the version of the mapping already on main", but .github/workflows/ci.yml:90-92 checks out with no `ref:` — on a pull_request that is refs/pull/N/merge, i.e. PR-authored content — and ci.yml:105 runs `node ./scripts/changed-areas.mjs` from that tree, which reads harness.config.json from the same checkout (changed-areas.mjs:86-93, REPO_ROOT). The resolver is also the sole computer of the `ciConfig` escape hatch (changed-areas.mjs:387-400), so a PR editing the resolver decides whether its own edit is flagged; the documented anti-self-grading property is therefore not implemented. The exploit chain is complete in-repo: `changes.outputs.areas` flows to verify-self as WAFFLEBASE_CHANGED_AREAS (ci.yml:228); resolve() returns a supplied object verbatim when isResolution() passes (changed-areas.mjs:510-527), and {"full":false,"packages":[],"tags":[]} satisfies that shape check, making selectLaneNames select zero lanes (changed-areas.mjs:581-595); verify-browser and verify-integration gate every step on RUN_HEAVY (ci.yml:414-417,434,440 and 523-526,556,562) and report success under the required matrix names by design. Result: three green required contexts with nothing executed. I looked for a guard that would make this unreachable and did not find a mechanical one: .github/CODEOWNERS:53-61 owns harness.config.json and scripts/changed-areas.mjs, but the same file states at lines 16-26 and 50-52 that no repo-wide rule is set and that CODEOWNERS only blocks a merge once "Require review from Code Owners" is enabled in branch protection, which is not verifiable in-repo. The `ci-config-changed` label — the loud reviewer-facing signal — is itself derived from the PR-produced areas.json (ci-report.yml:157, 276-289) and is now removable via ci-report.yml:284, so the compensating control is computed by the same untrusted data it polices. The only refutation I could construct is that a PR author can already force green CI by editing verify-self.mjs or the tests; that argues the weakness is not novel, not that it is absent or unreachable, so it does not meet the bar to drop this from the merge gate. This is a weakened merge/authorization gate documented as a control it does not enforce — squarely in the security lane, major impact as filed.
